_source: docs/BENCHMARKS.md BENCH-VK-LLAMA row; .agents/benchmark-record.md 'BACKEND-VULKAN combined'. Every number here is a MEASURED binding value, not a projection.
title: Vulkan decode meets llama.cpp on a 27B
workload: 7 clean legs with the host page cache dropped before each and the GPU serialized under one lock, one leg discarded for a NAMED cause (an overlapping compile job, not the unexplained 1-in-16 collapse); llama.cpp built -DGGML_VULKAN=ON at 237ad9b96 with a from-source shaderc so all five of its Vulkan fast paths report supported (banner: matrix cores NV_coopmat2), llama-bench tg1024, same weights
headline: 4.36 vs 4.35 tok/s, MET (denominator SUPERSEDED)
subline: our GPU-side work was already ahead of llama.cpp's wall clock; pipelined submission closed the host-side remainder
footnotes: Decode tokens/s per stream. Ours is the median of 7 clean legs, TPOT 228.66 to 230.25 ms, spread 0.69% -- that spread IS the noise floor, so this is a narrow pass, not a comfortable one. llama.cpp is llama-bench tg1024 at 4.35 +- 0.00.

OPERATOR CORROBORATION, stated at its real strength: an independent run on a different main SHA, with its own fresh configure, read 4.58 tok/s -- but n=1, on a freshly rebooted box with clean memory, so it is treated as OPTIMISTIC and the 7-leg median is the binding figure. It confirms the direction, not the value. Further legs were abandoned rather than reboot the box a third time.

The campaign arc on this model: decode 2.40 -> 4.36 tok/s. The levers, in order of size: RMSNorm was dispatching ONE workgroup per row at batch 1 (7.85 -> 1.59 ms/token), GDN state I/O moved in place, the fused attention preamble went native (16 host round trips per token removed), the command batch stopped draining on every host memcpy, lm_head got column blocking, and submission was pipelined.

The GEMV lever is CLOSED with its binding constraint identified: DRAM bandwidth on a ~50 GB working set streamed once per token, at 248.0 GB/s. llama.cpp's own rows-per-workgroup trick measured 0.966x here and ships off.
Prefill is 21.5x its pre-campaign value on the same model. opt-125m greedy stays STRICT token-exact against the vLLM 0.25.0 oracle with 0 declines.
llama.cpp's own CUDA arm on this box is 4.67 tok/s, so its Vulkan backend runs at 93% of its CUDA.

DENOMINATOR SUPERSEDED (2026-08-16). 237ad9b96 is our own local-only fork of llama.cpp, 65 of this project's performance commits past upstream tag b9827, and it exists on no remote: the GitHub API answers 'No commit found for SHA' for both mudler/llama.cpp and ggml-org/llama.cpp. The tree it was built from also carried 27 uncommitted entries, so the binary is unidentified. None of the 65 commits touch ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/, so the compared Vulkan sources match b9827, but the build is still not reproducible. The oracle is now stock b10451 (10bf611e5). This is the FIRST verdict a re-take can flip: the 0.23% margin sits inside the 0.69% spread recorded in the first footnote. Re-take owed under #1003, and the pin is gateable=no until #857 builds it.
